headline: Island Bought to Stop Clear-Cutting Becomes Conservation Training Ground
meta_description: A 330-acre Maine island purchased to prevent clear-cutting now serves as a conservation training sanctuary, continuing Audubon's 90-year legacy.
summary_short: One woman's decision to buy a Maine island to stop clear-cutting has preserved a 330-acre sanctuary where conservationists continue their work.
body:
A woman purchased a Maine island to prevent clear-cutting, preserving what has become a vital training ground for the next generation of conservationists. The 330-acre sanctuary continues work that began nearly a century ago when Audubon opened its first camp on the island.

Ninety years after that original Audubon camp launched, the island remains dedicated to its conservation mission. What started as one person's effort to protect the land from logging has evolved into an active center where conservationists learn and develop their skills.

The story reflects how individual action—buying land to save it—can create lasting legacies. By stopping the clear-cutting that threatened the island, the purchase preserved not just trees and habitat, but also an institutional space where conservation education thrives.

Audubon opened first camp there 90 years ago
